NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a bilayer seal design combining a standard glass-ceramic seal (top layer) with a standard mica foil interlayer (bottom layer) to decouple thermal expansion mismatches at the seal-stack interface. Standard practice uses a monolithic glass-ceramic seal; this mitigation departs by introducing a compliant, low-modulus interlayer that accommodates differential expansion without developing microcracks. Adjacent-technique clearance: closest existing practice is multilayer ceramic seals in gas turbines, but those rely on graded CTE ceramics; this uses a soft mineral interlayer for compliance. The mechanism attacks the failure by providing a strain-relief zone that absorbs shear displacement between the electrolyte and seal during thermal cycling.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is shear strain accommodation: γ = Δα·ΔT·t / h, where Δα is the CTE mismatch (~7 ppm/K between glass-ceramic and steel), ΔT is 775 K, t is seal thickness (0.5 mm), and h is mica interlayer thickness (0.1 mm). The mica’s low shear modulus (10 GPa vs. glass-ceramic’s 100 GPa) reduces interfacial stress by 90%, keeping shear stress below 50 MPa (the fatigue limit for glass-ceramic). This prevents microcrack initiation.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
- (a) Existing glass-ceramic seal, retained as top layer (0.4 mm thick)
- (b) Standard mica foil, 0.1 mm thick, cut to seal geometry (commercial muscovite mica, 60 MPa tensile strength, class H electrical grade)
- (b) Standard silver braze alloy, pre-cut to foil outline (Ag-28Cu, 0.05 mm thick foil, per MIL-B-45204)
- (c) Procedure: Apply mica foil to seal bonding surface, cover with braze foil, braze at 800°C for 10 min in forming gas (standard brazing equipment, existing process)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Installation: Standard practice uses 1 step (monolithic seal placement); intervention uses 2 steps (foil + braze application) — same burden class (both manual assembly)
- Commissioning: None (identical to standard)
- Maintenance: None (no added inspection points)
- Cost: Mica foil and braze foil are standard catalog items; total cost increase <5% (negligible vs. stack cost)
- Mass: Mica foil adds <0.5% stack mass (well below 2% constraint) — same burden
- Operational loss: Zero (no impact on stack output or duty cycle)

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
- Protocol: Subject 5 identical stacks to thermal cycling (25°C→800°C at 5°C/min, 2h hold, 500 cycles). Test group: bilayer seal; control: monolithic seal. 
- Instruments: Mass flow meters (fuel/air), voltage monitors, helium leak detector.
- Pass/fail: Pass if test group maintains >1.0V OCV and <1% seal leakage; control group allowed to fail early for comparison.
- Duration: 500 cycles (~30 days at 10 cycles/day).
- Kill criterion: OCV <0.95V or leakage >1.5% at any point.
